chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Nayki, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Bashr ibn Maslamah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

Regarding a lamb that suckled from a sow and then was mixed with the sheep, he said: 'It is in the position of cheese; so if you know that it was mixed with it, do not eat it, and if you do not know that, then eat it.'

key_terms.الْجُبْنِ: Cheese (used as an analogy for mixed/impure substance)
key_terms.ضُرِبَ: Was mixed/struck (idiom for being mixed with a group)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from an animal that suckled from a different species?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the application of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in determining the permissibility of meat from cross-species nursing, specifically using the analogy of cheese to highlight how the source of nourishment affects the final product. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to resolving uncertainty in food consumption by distinguishing between definite knowledge of contamination and mere possibility. The ruling underscores the practical principle that in cases of doubt regarding an animal's lineage or diet, the default state of permissibility (*al-asl al-suhha*) prevails unless proven otherwise.
